reason: The passage (Exodus 1:6-12) describes a new Pharaoh who, motivated by fear of the Israelite population, implements an oppressive policy of enslavement and forced labor. Rather than governing for the benefit of the people, this regime subjugates a minority population, extracting their labor to build storage cities. The text is critical of this approach—it shows the policy as self-defeating (the more the Israelites are afflicted, the more they multiply) and ultimately harmful even to the Egyptians themselves (who become vexed by the situation). The passage presents an exemplar of poor, fear-based autocratic governance characterized by xenophobia and oppression, not a model of good leadership or functioning government benefiting the people.
